text.title: RFC Template for Product Dev Team — Worked Example
text.summary: One complete RFC for cutting checkout p95 from 2.4 s to 1.2 s (three options, five blast-radius items with owners, flag-off rollback exercised in staging, three milestones in five weeks, three named reviewers, accepted after the deadline, outcome re-measured at 1.1 s) with a note on each non-obvious value, then the "move to GraphQL" RFC and what the validator prints.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: acme/checkout. Mobile checkout p95 sits at 2.4 s over the last week and 18 percent of mobile sessions abandon on the payment step. swe:alice writes RFC-118 on 2026-05-29, proposing to precompute cart totals into the shared `orders` table behind a `checkout_v2` flag; swe:bob writes RFC-119 the same day proposing to move checkout to GraphQL.

example.title: RFC-118 checkout p95 under 1.2 s
example.note: `problem` has the metric with its source, 2.4 s today, 1.2 s by 2026-07-15, and a statement about abandonment rather than about a technology (r-problem-states-metric-and-target). Three options: the chosen precompute, a Redis cache rejected because the spike test stopped at 1.8 s, and do-nothing rejected on the abandonment cost (r-two-options-with-rejection-reasons). Five blast-radius items each carry an owner; the shared `orders` table and the billing job belong to swe:olena, which is why she is a reviewer; the mobile API and user segment carry counts (r-blast-radius-enumerated). Rollback is the flag off in one minute by the checkout on-call, exercised in staging run 88412, and the backfill is the point of no return with a row-count pre-check (r-rollback-named-timed-and-tested). Three milestones from 2026-06-12 to 2026-07-03 span three weeks; each is something a reviewer can query or see (r-scope-fits-one-cycle-with-milestones). The deadline 2026-06-04 is four working days after sharing on Friday 2026-05-29; the RFC was accepted on 2026-06-05, after the deadline, with product:maria not having commented, which the rule allows (r-reviewers-named-with-comment-deadline). The decision is one sentence naming the chosen option (r-decision-has-status-and-supersession). `next_review_at` 2026-08-07 is 35 days after ship and the outcome re-measured p95 at 1.1 s with the same dashboard: `met` (r-outcome-review-remeasures-problem-metric).

example.title: RFC-119 move checkout to GraphQL
example.note: What the validator prints: `problem.current_value` and `target_value` carry no number and the statement says "migrate to" (r-problem-states-metric-and-target); `options` has one entry (r-two-options-with-rejection-reasons); `milestones` has one entry named "launch" (r-scope-fits-one-cycle-with-milestones); reviewer `team:backend` is a team alias (r-reviewers-named-with-comment-deadline); `decision` is two sentences (r-decision-has-status-and-supersession); cross-field: the deadline is one day after sharing and the RFC was accepted before it passed with no comments (fm-approval-by-silence); `schema_change` and `data_backfill` are true with no point of no return and the rollback was never exercised (fm-rollback-is-a-sentence); the ship milestone is 124 days out (fm-four-month-rfc); `next_review_at` is far beyond one cycle after ship (r-outcome-review-remeasures-problem-metric). What the reviewer sees: a public API change on a shared table with the author as the only listed owner (fm-blast-radius-low).
